subject: MAP sprint charter: GPU pool sizing & close timeline (AtlasAI)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Park <jonathan.park@atlasai.com>; marissa_cole@redwood.com; rishi_malhotra@redwood.com; monica_patel@redwood.com; markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-15T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: MAP sprint charter: GPU pool sizing & close timeline (AtlasAI)

Jonathan / team —

Thanks again for the productive demos last week. As discussed, I’m starting a short MAP sprint to align on dedicated capacity sizing, throughput targets, and the close timeline so we can lock a reserved pool for AtlasAI before the end of Q2. I’ve attached a draft MAP and a preliminary capacity spreadsheet to kick things off.

High-level objectives for this MAP sprint (2 weeks):
- Agree on 95th/99th token latency targets and throughput baseline (tokens/sec / concurrent requests)
- Finalize GPU pool size & burst policy for launch week
- Align procurement checklist + target signature date
- Define stakeholder owners and escalation paths

Proposed timeline:
- Today (Mar 15): internal kickoff & send draft to AtlasAI
- Mar 17: joint stakeholder sync (30m) to confirm throughput/SLAs
- Mar 22: procurement paperwork ready for review
- Mar 29: target contract signature (can be earlier with expedited procurement)

Immediate asks for AtlasAI: can you confirm the 3-week production pilot window and the expected peak concurrency during that window (e.g., 200 concurrent chat sessions, 40 req/s)? That will help the capacity sheet.

Internal owners (please confirm):
- Marissa Cole — MAP project lead (schedule, documentation)
- Rishi Malhotra — capacity planning & throughput targets
- Monica Patel — security & compliance intake (SOC2 evidence, network)
- Markus Klein — edge routing + region placement (us-east / us-west)

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (map outline), capacity-estimate-AtlasAI.xlsx (working numbers), SLA-proposal-AtlasAI.docx

Thanks — looking forward to a quick cadence here.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Jonathan Park <jonathan.park@atlasai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; marissa_cole@redwood.com; rishi_malhotra@redwood.com; monica_patel@redwood.com; markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-15T11:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP sprint charter: GPU pool sizing & close timeline (AtlasAI)

Hi Ben — thanks for the note and the attachments. Quick answers:
- We can do a 3-week production pilot starting Apr 10.
- Expected peak: ~150 concurrent chat sessions, burst to 300 for a few hours during marketing events. Sustained throughput ~35 req/s, average payload ~250 tokens/request.

Procurement: I’m looping in our procurement alias (copied) — we typically need 10 business days once the SOW and invoice are signed. If you can get the SOW to us by Mar 22, we should be able to close by Mar 29 as you suggested.

Also, can Rishi confirm if the preliminary capacity sheet accounts for KV-cache efficiency with prefix caching? That matters because our prompt design uses a long shared prefix.

Best,
Jonathan
Head of Product | AtlasAI
jonathan.park@atlasai.com

- Rishi: updated capacity sheet with prefix-caching assumptions + burst policy scenarios (p95/p99 projections)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; Jonathan Park <jonathan.park@atlasai.com>; monica_patel@redwood.com; markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-15T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP sprint charter: GPU pool sizing & close timeline (AtlasAI)

Quick read of their numbers — good catch on the prefix cache question. Notes: 
- I updated capacity-estimate-AtlasAI.xlsx with two scenarios:
  * Scenario A (conservative): assume prefix cache hit 10% — baseline 8 A100s (or equivalent instances) to meet p95 < 250ms and sustain 35 req/s with 150 concurrent sessions.
  * Scenario B (optimized): assume prefix cache hit 45% — baseline 5 A100s with burst pool of 2 instances to cover 300 concurrent bursts.
- p99 latency projections are sensitive to sequence length; I included 8 tokens/sec generation baseline and a separate column for 2x longer sequences.

I’ll pull the charts for Mar 17 and include a short note on cost delta between the scenarios so AtlasAI can pick trade-offs.

-Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
